payload.task_text:
I am a PhD student preparing a survey presentation on recent advances in natural language processing, specifically focusing on large language models and their reasoning capabilities. I need to gather information from multiple sources, organize it systematically, and create both a data spreadsheet and a presentation.

First, visit the survey methodology guide at http://localhost:30231 to learn about how to structure a literature survey. The main page explains the overall approach including comparison criteria and taxonomy development. There is also a guide page at http://localhost:30231/guide.html with tips on presenting survey results effectively. Take notes on the recommended structure and presentation tips.

Next, search the arxiv paper database for recent papers related to NLP, language models, and reasoning. You should find around five relevant papers on these topics. For each paper, look up its full details including the abstract and read its LaTeX source to extract the key methodology, the datasets used in experiments, and the main findings. The LaTeX source of each paper (its section headings and content) is available through the arxiv-latex tools (list_paper_sections, get_paper_section, get_paper_prompt). In the content returned by these tools, each section heading appears on its own line starting with '#', so you can count the sections of a paper by counting those heading lines (or by reading the sections list returned by list_paper_sections). Count the LaTeX sections of each paper, because the survey needs the average number of sections across papers.

After gathering all the paper information, create an Excel workbook called Survey_Data.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be named "Paper Comparison" with columns Paper_ID, Title, Year, Method, Dataset, and Key_Finding. The Paper_ID column must contain each paper's arXiv identifier in the standard form YYMM.NNNNN (for example 2404.00001), with no prefix such as "arXiv:" and no version suffix such as "v1". The Method column should describe the core approach in a few words, the Dataset column should list the primary evaluation dataset, and Key_Finding should summarize the main result. The second sheet should be named "Taxonomy" with columns Category and Papers. Group the papers into meaningful categories based on their approaches such as prompting methods, training methods, and architectural innovations. The third sheet should be named "Summary Statistics" with columns Metric and Value, including Total_Papers, Most_Common_Category, Year_Range, and Average_Sections (average number of LaTeX sections across papers). All values in the Value column must be written as literal text or numbers in the cell itself — do NOT write Excel formulas (for example, do not enter "=COUNTA(...)" or "=AVERAGE(...)"; instead write the plain number, e.g. 5 or 4.0).

Then create a PowerPoint presentation called NLP_Survey.pptx in the workspace. The presentation should have at least six slides. The first slide should be a title slide with a title containing the words "NLP Survey" or "Language Model Survey" or similar. The second slide should present the survey methodology and structure based on what you learned from the methodology guide. Then include one slide for each of at least three key papers, showing the paper title, its method, dataset, and key finding. End with a summary slide that provides a taxonomy overview and identifies key trends across the surveyed papers.

Please review the survey outline and presentation style guide files in the workspace for additional context about the expected structure and formatting guidelines.

Important coordination note: this is a multi-agent task and all agents share the same workspace. Each of the two final files (Survey_Data.xlsx and NLP_Survey.pptx) must be written to disk by a single sub-agent. Never have more than one agent write the same file at the same time — concurrent writes to the same file overwrite each other. Coordinate your work so that, after the research information has been gathered, one designated sub-agent is responsible for writing Survey_Data.xlsx and one (or the same agent) is responsible for writing NLP_Survey.pptx.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must list and read all task-visible survey-outline and presentation-style reference files in read-only mode, without assuming their filenames, and freeze the survey comparison schema, taxonomy/statistics rules, at-least-six-slide contract, and single-writer ownership of Survey_Data.xlsx and NLP_Survey.pptx. It must resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. It must then inspect the granted runtime tool catalog and verify that the task-required LaTeX section operations can actually read section lists and contents for discovered paper IDs. If those operations are unavailable or no authorized source can return the required paper bodies, the main agent must stop before delegation, report the exact missing-capability blocker, and must not fabricate Method, Dataset, Key_Finding, section counts, or either dependent deliverable. The following waves apply only when the required source capability is present; all paper facts must come from task-visible runtime sources.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to inspect both task-provided survey-methodology pages in read-only mode and combine their source-backed guidance with the frozen local-reference packet supplied by the main agent. Use only the granted non-interactive browser navigation, snapshot, search, and wait operations; do not click, type, evaluate scripts, select options, invoke terminal, or reread workspace files. Return a compact source-referenced methodology packet covering comparison criteria, taxonomy guidance, recommended presentation structure, slide tips, and per-page/reference coverage. Do not write deliverables or alter the pages.

   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to scout the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space read-only for recent NLP, language-model, and reasoning papers. Use complementary queries at the supported per-call result bound, union and deduplicate by stable ID because no search cursor is exposed, validate relevance from title/abstract, and return a candidate manifest with authors/date, abstract, available arxiv-latex status, per-query/union controls, and rejected distractors. Do not read full manuscripts, write files, or create deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent must apply the task's relevance rule, select exactly five source-supported papers, and freeze an explicit five-row assignment table containing `agent_no`, stable ID, and exact title, with one distinct paper per row.

Before dispatching Wave 2, render each numbered prompt into a complete self-contained instruction that includes that row's literal stable ID and exact title, the permitted read-only paper/LaTeX calls, the complete return schema and all missing/conflict controls. Never send an agent only an ordinal such as "paper row 3" or require it to infer fields from another prompt.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 5 explore sub-agents in parallel, one for each frozen paper:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 1 from the frozen assignment table.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 2 from the frozen assignment table.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 3): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 3 from the frozen assignment table.
   4. explore 3 (academic-literature-researcher 4): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 4 from the frozen assignment table.
   5. explore 4 (academic-literature-researcher 5): Use one explore sub-agent to own only paper row 5 from the frozen assignment table.

Each Wave 2 sub-agent must process only its one assigned stable ID/title, retrieve full metadata, read the available arxiv-latex source and sections, count sections from the returned section list or heading lines, and extract source-backed core method, primary dataset, and key finding. Return one compact paper record with exact normalized ID, provenance, section count, source controls, and missing/conflict status. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create Excel or PowerPoint.

After Wave 2, the main agent must verify the five assigned IDs each appear exactly once, calculate Total_Papers, taxonomy membership, Most_Common_Category, Year_Range, and literal Average_Sections, and freeze one literal canonical survey dataset plus the methodology packet. Both artifact owners consume the same payload without recomputing taxonomy, section counts, or paper facts.

3. Wave 3 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own `<workspace_root>/Survey_Data.xlsx` exclusively. Use one `python_execute` with `openpyxl` to create Paper Comparison, Taxonomy, and Summary Statistics atomically from the canonical payload with exact headers, standard IDs without prefix/version, literal Value cells, source-backed method/dataset/finding rows, and verified taxonomy/statistics. Then read each complete populated range once and return path, sheet order, row/metric controls, and validation. Do not write the presentation.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own `<workspace_root>/NLP_Survey.pptx` exclusively. Use one `python_execute` with `python-pptx` to create the complete deck atomically from the canonical payload, with at least six slides including a title slide, methodology slide grounded in the webpage/guide packet, at least three distinct paper slides, and a final taxonomy/trends summary. Follow the visible style guide, then read the deck once and return path, slide count/titles, paper/methodology coverage, and validation. Do not write the workbook.

After Wave 3, the main agent must reconcile paper IDs, methods, datasets, findings, taxonomy, and statistics between both files and verify single-writer provenance and readability before completion.

nodes.text:
Your task is to create an Excel workbook file called Survey_Data.xlsx at this absolute path:

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_claude-sonnet-5/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-survey-presentation/workspace/Survey_Data.xlsx

It must contain exactly THREE worksheets named "Paper Comparison", "Taxonomy", and "Summary Statistics". Use the mcp__excel__ tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, delete_worksheet, rename_worksheet) to build it. A new workbook starts with a default "Sheet1" — rename it to "Paper Comparison" (or delete it and create the three sheets you need).

=== SHEET 1: "Paper Comparison" ===
Columns (header row): Paper_ID, Title, Year, Method, Dataset, Key_Finding
Rows (one per paper, 5 rows of data):

1. Paper_ID=2404.00001 | Title=Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Complex Reasoning | Year=2024 | Method=Chain-of-thought prompting | Dataset=GSM8K, MATH | Key_Finding=15% improvement on GSM8K and 12% on MATH over standard prompting
2. Paper_ID=2404.00002 | Title=Instruction Tuning for Improved Language Understanding | Year=2024 | Method=Instruction tuning with LoRA | Dataset=MMLU, BBH, TriviaQA | Key_Finding=10B model reaches 72.5% on MMLU, outperforming models 5x larger
3. Paper_ID=2404.00003 | Title=Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP | Year=2024 | Method=Retrieval-augmented generation | Dataset=Natural Questions, TriviaQA | Key_Finding=40% reduction in hallucination on knowledge-intensive tasks
4. Paper_ID=2404.00004 | Title=Self-Consistency in Language Model Reasoning | Year=2024 | Method=Self-consistency decoding | Dataset=GSM8K, SVAMP, AQuA | Key_Finding=8% improvement on GSM8K over standard chain-of-thought
5. Paper_ID=2404.00005 | Title=Multimodal Large Language Models for Visual Reasoning | Year=2024 | Method=Visual instruction tuning (CLIP + LLaMA) | Dataset=VQA v2, COCO captioning | Key_Finding=State-of-the-art on VQA, visual dialogue, and image captioning

Paper_ID values MUST be exactly the bare arXiv IDs (e.g. 2404.00001) — no "arXiv:" prefix, no "v1" version suffix. Year should be written as a literal number 2024. Do not use any Excel formulas anywhere in the workbook.

=== SHEET 2: "Taxonomy" ===
Columns: Category, Papers
Rows:
1. Category=Prompting Methods | Papers=2404.00001, 2404.00004
2. Category=Training Methods | Papers=2404.00002, 2404.00005
3. Category=Architectural Innovations | Papers=2404.00003

=== SHEET 3: "Summary Statistics" ===
Columns: Metric, Value
Rows (all values must be LITERAL text or numbers typed into the cell — never Excel formulas like =COUNTA() or =AVERAGE()):
1. Metric=Total_Papers | Value=5
2. Metric=Most_Common_Category | Value=Prompting Methods
3. Metric=Year_Range | Value=2024
4. Metric=Average_Sections | Value=4.0

After writing, VERIFY the workbook by reading it back with get_workbook_metadata and read_data_from_excel on each sheet, and confirm: exactly 3 sheets with the correct names, correct headers, 5 paper rows, and that the Summary Statistics Value cells contain literal values (not formulas). Report the final absolute file path and a summary of what you wrote. Do NOT modify any other files.
Write Survey_Data.xlsx workbook

Your task is to create a PowerPoint presentation file called NLP_Survey.pptx at this absolute path:

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_claude-sonnet-5/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-survey-presentation/workspace/NLP_Survey.pptx

Use the mcp__pptx__ tools (create_presentation, add_slide, populate_placeholder, add_bullet_points, add_table, set_core_properties, save_presentation). The presentation must have AT LEAST SIX slides, in this order:

SLIDE 1 — Title slide: A title slide whose title contains the words "NLP Survey" (e.g. "NLP Survey: Recent Advances in Reasoning with Large Language Models"). Add a subtitle line such as "A Survey of Prompting, Training, and Architectural Methods" and an author line identifying it as a PhD student survey.

SLIDE 2 — Survey methodology and structure (based on the methodology guide). Use bullet points covering: the research question(s) (how have LLMs improved reasoning recently; what are the main methodological approaches — prompting, training, or architecture; which benchmarks are most used); the comparison criteria (methodology type, evaluation benchmark/dataset, reported improvement over baseline, model scale); and the taxonomy approach (grouping by primary method: prompting vs training vs architecture). Mention that comparison tables and a taxonomy overview are used.

SLIDE 3 — Key Paper 1: Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Complex Reasoning (arXiv 2404.00001, 2024). Content: Method = chain-of-thought prompting (step-by-step reasoning demonstrations, few-shot with 4-8 examples); Dataset = GSM8K, MATH; Key finding = 15% improvement on GSM8K and 12% on MATH vs standard prompting.

SLIDE 4 — Key Paper 2: Instruction Tuning for Improved Language Understanding (arXiv 2404.00002, 2024). Content: Method = instruction tuning with LoRA (rank 64) over 50K instruction-response pairs spanning 200 task categories; Dataset = MMLU, BBH, TriviaQA; Key finding = a 10B model reaches 72.5% on MMLU, outperforming models 5x larger.

SLIDE 5 — Key Paper 3: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP (arXiv 2404.00003, 2024). Content: Method = retrieval-augmented generation (dense retrieval with contriever + fine-tuned LLaMA generator, top-5 passages); Dataset = Natural Questions, TriviaQA; Key finding = 40% reduction in hallucination on knowledge-intensive tasks.

SLIDE 6 — Summary / taxonomy overview and key trends. Present the taxonomy: Prompting Methods (Chain-of-Thought 2404.00001, Self-Consistency 2404.00004), Training Methods (Instruction Tuning 2404.00002, Visual Instruction Tuning 2404.00005), Architectural Innovations (Retrieval-Augmented Generation 2404.00003). Then list key trends across the surveyed papers: (1) prompting and decoding techniques (CoT, self-consistency) improve reasoning without retraining; (2) instruction/tuning methods boost generalization and efficiency beyond scale alone; (3) retrieval grounding reduces hallucination on factual tasks; (4) benchmarks cluster around reasoning (GSM8K, MATH) and knowledge-intensive QA (MMLU, TriviaQA, Natural Questions); (5) multimodal extensions broaden the scope. Optionally add 2-3 open questions for future work.

Optionally you may add a small comparison table on the summary slide (Paper_ID | Method | Dataset | Key metric) using add_table. Keep text concise and bullet-based (avoid long paragraphs) per the presentation style guide. Use a consistent color scheme and a clear title on each slide.

After saving, VERIFY by extracting the presentation text (extract_presentation_text) and confirming there are at least 6 slides and the required elements are present. Report the final absolute file path and a per-slide summary of content. Do NOT modify any other files.
Write NLP_Survey.pptx presentation
